evidence.B8: Scope is bounded by an authoritative contract and fixed CLI/output ("SPEC.md ... is authoritative for rendering, scoring, generation, output rows, and metrics", `--out /app/results.json`), which limits over-building. But the ask is an open-ended "Repair" of an unknown number of latent bugs across rendering, scoring, generation, batching and caching, with a standing temptation to make modes agree by special-casing — the instruction pre-empts exactly this with "Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task" and "This CLI must work for any valid shard".
evidence.C2: `expertMinutes: 1440` (24 hours) and a 4-hour agent budget; per the C2 ladder, over ~8 hours means mandatory per-step stops are a rounding error against the work.
evidence.C4: The deliverable and interface are fully named (exact CLI invocation, `--out /app/results.json`, SPEC.md authoritative), but the instruction never says what is broken — the approach cannot be chosen until the supplied inputs named in the instruction (`/app/evalbench/`, `SPEC.md`, `/app/model/`, `public_eval.jsonl`, `public_runtime.jsonl`) are inspected and the defects located. Profile level 2, not 3, because a concrete deliverable and contract are stated rather than a bare symptom.

rows.processRecommendation: library/methodologies/tdd.js composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js (gates: the sample CLI invocation, a batch-size/padding-side/order invariance sweep asserting identical results.json, a cold-vs-warm --cache-dir run, and a timed run over public_runtime.jsonl)
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent reads part of SPEC.md, fixes the obvious padded-mode bug (e.g. attention mask / position ids under left padding), runs the sample command on `public_eval.jsonl` once, sees plausible metrics in `/app/results.json` and declares done — never sweeping batch size × padding side × input order for invariance, never re-running with a pre-warmed `--cache-dir` to prove "correctness must not depend on prior cache contents", and never exercising `public_runtime.jsonl` to confirm packed mode has not silently degraded to per-example recomputation. The alternative concrete failure: it forces packed to agree with padded by special-casing the packed path, so both modes are consistently wrong relative to the single-example model semantics.
rows.rationale: The decisive factor is horizon: 1440 expert-minutes and a 14400-second agent budget put this well past one sitting, which drives B3 to 3 and C2 to 0, so orchestration overhead is negligible against the work. The instruction supplies an unusually rich set of self-measurable invariants — packed==padded, determinism, invariance to batch size, padding side and order, cache-independence, plus a named perf smoke shard — exactly the checklist a vanilla session verifies partially before declaring done (B5=2, B8=2). B1 earns 2 for the one real chained dependency: single-example semantics must be pinned against the model before batching is tuned to match it, or the parity fix is plausible-but-wrong. Costs stay low because SPEC.md is authoritative and the CLI/output contract is fixed; C4=2 only because the defects must be located by inspection before any approach can be chosen. B6 is low — one evaluator with many invariants, not genuine fan-out.

rows.name: biped-contact-dynamics

evidence.B1: The instruction names a natural reading order — "The notes in `/app/README_2DBiped.md` summarize the model coordinates, actuator/contact ordering, and useful PyDrake dynamics APIs" and "The visible config is `/app/configs/visible.json`" — but no step consumes an artifact produced by an earlier step. `walk.npz`, `jump.npz`, `run.npz` can be produced in any order; the starter script is explicitly optional ("you may use it as a reference or ignore it entirely"). No chained artifact dependency.
evidence.B3: `expertMinutes: 300` (5 hours, above the 120-minute corpus median) and `agentTimeoutSec: 14400`, well above the 7200 threshold in the profile ladder. The instruction itself states "You have 14400 seconds to complete this task." Three distinct trajectories plus a full multibody-dynamics consistency implementation.
evidence.B5: Dense set of self-measurable numeric targets: "trapezoidal residual below `0.005`", "center-of-mass force-balance residual must remain below `100 N`", "floating-base and full inverse-dynamics residuals must remain below `30`", "contact-force rate must remain below `8000 N/s`", "actuator-torque rate must remain below `3500 N·m/s`", "more than `0.12 m` of clearance", "6 cm or more", "the 10th percentile of base x-velocity must stay above 40% of its mean", plus the stated aggregation (exclude first/last 3 samples, 5-sample margin at mode transitions, 95th-percentile). The agent can reimplement these locally and correct toward them. Not 3: these are pass/fail tolerances, not a stated minimise-error or beat-a-baseline loop with headroom.
evidence.B6: Three separately-specified, separately-verifiable artifacts — "`walk.npz` must contain a forward walk…", "`jump.npz` must contain a vertical jump…", "`run.npz` must contain a forward running gait…" — each with its own mode-sequence and clearance requirements, plus hidden-config reruns. Real fan-out, but all three share one generator, one model, and one dynamics/consistency core ("Each `.npz` file must contain arrays named `t`, `state`, `u`, `contact_forces`, and `mode`"), so not dozens of independent units.
evidence.B8: Wide latitude on method — "The chosen solution method (closed-form inverse dynamics, trajectory optimization, RL, etc.) is not constrained" — invites over-building (e.g. contact-implicit trajopt) against the 14400s budget, and generalisation is easy to silently skip: "hidden configs may change these values… do not hard-code only the visible trajectory" plus a 1200s per-invocation limit on runs the agent never sees. Held off 3 because the output surface is pinned exactly (array names, shapes `(K,14)`, `(K,4)`, `(K,)`, mode encoding `0/1/2/3`, actuator order `[left hip, right hip, left knee, right knee]`, ±500 torque bound) and the diff is one generator file.
evidence.C2: `expertMinutes: 300` falls in the profile's ~2–8 hour band; mandatory per-step stops are material but do not dominate five hours of PyDrake multibody work across three gaits plus hidden-config generalisation.
evidence.C4: Every deliverable and its format is enumerated up front — the CLI contract "python /app/submission/solve.py --config CONFIG_JSON --output OUTPUT_DIR", the three output files, the five arrays with shapes and orderings, and all numeric tolerances. Only the method is open ("closed-form inverse dynamics, trajectory optimization, RL, etc."), a tooling/approach choice within a standard robotics domain. Not 2: no supplied input must be inspected before the shape of the work is knowable — the README/URDF inform content, not shape.

rows.processRecommendation: custom — an iterative-convergence loop wrapping library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js, with the gate backed by a locally reimplemented residual/mode checker run over both the visible config and a perturbed one
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The likely vanilla failure is a premature "done" on the visible config: the agent gets `walk.npz` looking plausible against `/app/configs/visible.json`, never reimplements the verifier's aggregation locally (exclude first/last 3 samples, 5-sample margin around mode transitions, 95th percentile), and never re-runs `solve.py` on a second config — so the full inverse-dynamics residual quietly sits above 30 and the hidden-config reruns (hidden_jump.json, hidden_stride.json) either exceed 1200s or emit hard-coded timing. A second concrete skip: the run-gait mode structure ("`DOUBLE_SUPPORT` must not appear anywhere in the run trajectory", strict LEFT_STANCE→FLIGHT→RIGHT_STANCE alternation, two FLIGHT blocks of ≥12 samples with ≥6 cm clearance) gets asserted rather than measured once walk and jump appear to work.
rows.rationale: Horizon dominates the benefit side: 300 expert-minutes and a 14400s agent budget put B3 at 2, with a dense set of self-measurable tolerances (B5=2) and three separately-verifiable gait artifacts (B6=2) reinforcing it. Cost is low on both live dimensions — the work is long enough that orchestration stops are not the dominant expense (C2=1), and the deliverable is enumerated down to array names and shapes, so the shape is encodable even though the method is deliberately left open (C4=1). Drift risk is the interesting case: the task is hard, but difficulty is not drift — the exact output schema and the ±500/30/0.005 bounds constrain the agent tightly, so B8=2 rests on the unconstrained solution method and the easily-skipped hidden-config generalisation, not on the physics. Ordering is genuinely weak (B1=1): the three npz files and the listed requirements have no artifact-flow dependency between them. The counterfactual is concrete and is the main thing arguing for enforcement — a gate that re-runs the generator on a second config and recomputes the residuals is exactly what a vanilla session would skip.

rows.name: bun-sourcemap-leak

evidence.B1: Artifact flow is chained: the release must first read `/app/visibility.json` as the provenance policy, then emit `/app/dist/client-entry.js.map`, then scrub it ('If an emitted source map contains both public and private sources, preserve mappings for public sources while removing private source provenance'), and finally emit `/app/dist/release-manifest.json` whose `artifacts` array and provenance describe the already-emitted files. Building the manifest or scrubbing before classification is available yields a plausible-but-wrong result.
evidence.B3: `expertMinutes: 90` and `agentTimeoutSec: 1800` — inside the ~30-120 minute band and far below the 7200s threshold for a 2.
evidence.B5: The instruction names self-runnable checks with exact expected output — `/app/dist/client-entry.js` must print exactly `Hello, Ada!`, `server-entry.js` must print exactly `PUBLIC_RESPONSE: Hello, Ada!`, and `--trace-probe` must report `PUBLIC_RENDER_PROBE` and resolve to `src/client/render.ts` — but no numeric target or tolerance with headroom to iterate toward.
evidence.B6: Three-ish coupled outputs from one pipeline (`client-entry.js` + `.map`, `server-entry.js`, `release-manifest.json`); they share the single `bun run release` build and one visibility policy, so they are not independently workable units. Not a fan-out of N verifiable targets.
evidence.B8: Latitude plus broad negative requirements invite both over-narrow and over-broad fixes: the pipeline must work for 'whatever input app is present in /app at runtime' (not the one app the agent can see), and requirement 5 forbids exposing 'server-only source contents, text from generated private modules, secret-bearing constants, private module identities, private source names, or local filesystem paths' — an open-ended leak surface. The easy over-correction (drop or inline the map) still satisfies the visible greeting checks, so a wrong result looks done.
evidence.C2: `expertMinutes: 90`, `agentTimeoutSec: 1800` — squarely in the ~30-120 minute band where per-step mandatory stops are a noticeable fraction of the total work.
evidence.C4: Outputs are enumerated precisely, but the approach cannot be chosen until supplied inputs named in the instruction are inspected: `/app/visibility.json`'s `publicSources`/`privateSources` shape, the existing `bun run release` pipeline and its current leak, and the existing client `--trace-probe` path. How to make sources 'resolve relative to the emitted `.map` file location' without `sourceRoot` depends on what Bun's bundler currently emits in this repo.

rows.processRecommendation: library/specializations/security-compliance/ composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent hardcodes the layout of the one app present in /app rather than deriving it from visibility.json at runtime, satisfies the two exact-output greeting checks, and declares success — producing a release pipeline that is silently wrong for any other input app; or it strips/inlines the source map to stop the leak, which passes the greeting checks while breaking the required deobfuscation to src/client/render.ts.
rows.rationale: The decisive factor is cost: a 90-expert-minute, single-pipeline task (C2=2) whose approach must be discovered by reading the existing release script and visibility policy (C4=2) carries orchestration overhead that the benefit side does not repay. On the benefit side only B1 does real work — the policy read, bundle emit, map scrub, and manifest form a genuine chain where out-of-order production yields a plausible-but-wrong artifact — and B8=2 because the runtime-generality requirement and the open-ended leak list make a hardcoded or map-deleting solution look finished. B3, B5, and B6 are all low: one sitting, no numeric target with headroom, one coupled artifact set. The counterfactual is concrete and non-empty, so no cap applies.

rows.name: cad-model

evidence.B1: Single transformation: "output a STEP file in `/app/out.step` which contains the object described by the 2d schematic in `/app/schematic.png`". Natural reading order (inspect schematic, then model, then export) but no named intermediate artifact that a later step consumes; deviating corrupts nothing silently.
evidence.B3: metadata `expertMinutes: 120` and `agentTimeoutSec: 7200`; the instruction states "You have 7200 seconds to complete this task." The profile ladder puts an agent timeout at/above 7200 at B3=2.
evidence.B5: The instruction names no self-runnable check, no tolerance, and no numeric target — only "the object described by the 2d schematic". Success is binary against a hidden verifier (`test_outputs.py`), with nothing stated to measure and iterate toward.
evidence.B6: One indivisible deliverable: a single file `/app/out.step` describing one object. No N files, N cases, or independently verifiable sub-targets are named.
evidence.B8: Output is exactly specified — one path (`/app/out.step`), one format (STEP), one object — which tightly bounds the blast radius. Latitude is in reading the drawing, so the realistic error is a wrong-but-plausible solid rather than sprawl; the instruction also fences scope with "Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task."
evidence.C2: `expertMinutes: 120` sits at the top of the profile's ~30–120 minute band; per-step mandatory stops are a noticeable fraction of a two-hour modeling job whose actual work is writing and re-running one CAD script.
evidence.C4: The deliverable and its location are named (`/app/out.step`, STEP, derived from `/app/schematic.png`) but no method is prescribed. The schematic's content is unknown until viewed, yet the shape of the work is standard for the stated domain (tags `cad`, `3d-modeling`): read the drawing, build the solid in a kernel, export STEP — only the tooling choice is open.

rows.processRecommendation: custom
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent reads a couple of dimensions off `schematic.png`, writes a CadQuery/OpenCASCADE script that produces a roughly-right solid, sees the file appear at `/app/out.step`, and declares done — without ever re-rendering its model back into the schematic's orthographic views and checking every dimension, so a missing hole, an omitted fillet, or a misread hidden-line feature ships as a plausible but wrong solid that still exports as valid STEP.
rows.rationale: The decisive factor is C2 against a thin benefit profile: this is a single-artifact, ~120-expert-minute modeling task whose only benefit signal above zero is horizon (B3=2, driven by the 7200s agent timeout stated in the instruction), and per-step orchestration stops are a material fraction of the work. B5=0 and B6=0 because the instruction exposes no measurable target and no fan-out — one object, one file. Drift risk is low (B8=1): the output path and format are exact, so the difficulty here is modeling accuracy, not scope sprawl, and the profile explicitly separates the two. C4 is 1 rather than 2 because the unreadable input makes the object's content unknown while leaving the shape of the work — read drawing, build solid, export STEP — entirely knowable. The counterfactual is concrete but modest: the realistic vanilla failure is under-verification against the drawing, which a gate could catch only if the agent first builds its own comparison, something the instruction never asks for.

rows.name: cargo-flight-dispatch

evidence.B1: "The planning code is split across three files: /app/navigation.py — distance, bearing, heading, wind triangle... /app/aircraft.py — airspeed, fuel burn, weight... /app/dispatch.py — route optimization, flight plan assembly". There is a natural bottom-up layering (nav results feed fuel/weight, which feed route assembly) and an implicit diagnose-before-fix reading order, but the instruction names no intermediate artifact that a later step consumes and the fixes can be landed in any order as long as all land.
evidence.B3: metadata expertMinutes: 150 (~2.5 hours), above the corpus median of 120; agentTimeoutSec 3600 is below the 7200 marker but the instruction spans four data files, three code files, and multiple defect classes (declination, antimeridian, crosswind, fuel reserve, weight limits).
evidence.B5: The instruction names a self-runnable check — "running `python /app/dispatch.py --output /output/flight_plan.json` produces a correct flight plan" and "The output flight plan must be deterministic — same inputs produce the same plan every run" — but states no numeric target, tolerance, or score to iterate toward; correctness is binary against a hidden verifier.
evidence.B6: Defect classes are largely independent and separately checkable: "distance, bearing, heading, wind triangle, and crosswind calculations", "airspeed, fuel burn, weight, and reserve computations", plus "route optimization" — three files with distinct concerns (magnetic declination conversion, antimeridian crossing, crosswind limits, fuel for no-refuel strips) that could be worked in parallel, though they converge on one output artifact.
evidence.B8: "there are bugs ranging from missing features that the data files support but the code ignores to incorrect computations" — the defect set is explicitly unenumerated, which invites both premature "done" after the obvious arithmetic fixes and over-building of features the data merely hints at. Countered somewhat by a single fixed invocation and one output file, keeping the reviewable surface narrow.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes 150 (~2.5 hours) falls in the ~2–8 hour band: per-step mandatory stops are material but do not dominate work of this size; scored consistently with B3=2.
evidence.C4: The deliverable and command are exact ("produces a correct flight plan" via a named CLI), but the work cannot be planned until the supplied inputs are read — "Read the code and the data files carefully" — and the framing is symptomatic ("Pilots report fuel estimates that don't match their manual calculations"). Which fixes are needed is discovered by inspecting airports.json/aircraft.json/weather.json against the three source files.

rows.processRecommendation: library/cradle/bugfix.js composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js (per-subsystem gate on navigation → aircraft → dispatch, plus a determinism gate running the CLI twice and diffing)
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent fixes the visible arithmetic bugs and declares success, leaving the data-supported-but-ignored features (magnetic declination applied to true headings, antimeridian wrap in the distance calculation, crosswind limit checks against runway headings) unimplemented, and ships a plausible flight_plan.json whose fuel reserves for the no-refuel island strips are still wrong.
rows.rationale: The decisive tension is a moderate horizon (150 expert-minutes, above corpus median) and an explicitly unenumerated defect set against an equally moderate shape uncertainty — the deliverable and invocation are exact, but which bugs exist is only discoverable by reading four data files and three source files. B3 and B8 carry the benefit: an agent working vanilla is most likely to fix the arithmetic it can see and never notice the declination, antimeridian, and crosswind features the data supports but the code ignores. B1 stays at 1 because the layering is a natural reading order, not a chained artifact dependency whose violation corrupts the output. C4=2 is the dominant cost: any process encoded up front would be guessing at the bug inventory, so enforcement helps mainly as a completeness sweep over named subsystems rather than as a fixed phase sequence. Benefit_live and Cost_live land near parity, so this sits close to the middle of the corpus distribution.

rows.name: cli-2ph-simplex

evidence.B1: Chained artifact flow is explicit: "apply them immediately after constructing the Phase 1 tableau"; "Artificial variable columns are removed at the end of Phase 1"; and the derived reports consume the end product — "in the final tableau, the problem is degenerate if any constraint row ... has an RHS of 0 within 1e-9" and the basic-variable report "must contain one valid final basis represented by the final tableau". Applying the initial pivots after canonicalization, or removing artificial columns at the wrong point, silently yields a plausible-but-wrong tableau. Not a 3 because the ordering lives inside one algorithm implementation rather than across separately-produced workflow steps.
evidence.B3: metadata expertMinutes 120 and agentTimeoutSec 2500 (~42 min) — the profile's ~30–120 minute band. No phase produces a durable artifact a later sitting must resume from; the whole thing is one package under /app.
evidence.B5: The instruction states a measurable optimisation target with headroom: "the total number of pivot-log entries, including the provided prefix pivots, is the smallest possible among all valid paths", explicitly warning that "Bland's rule, Dantzig's rule, or any other fixed pivot rule is not guaranteed to produce that required smallest total number of pivots" — the agent can enumerate valid paths and measure its own count down. A concrete tolerance is also given ("RHS of 0 within 1e-9"). Not a 3 because no numeric target value or baseline is stated for the agent to check itself against.
evidence.B6: The starter package is pre-split — "/app/simplex/parser.py, /app/simplex/phases.py, /app/simplex/schema.py, and /app/simplex/tableau.py" — and the problem-report formatter (§2) is genuinely independent of the solver. But the four output artifacts all derive from one final tableau produced by one CLI entrypoint; this is one indivisible deliverable with a few separable pieces, not fan-out.
evidence.B8: Output shapes are pinned tightly ("exact schema {\"step\": int, \"phase\": int, ...}", "exact signature {\"degenerate\": bool}", "Z at index 0 and RHS at the last index"), which caps over-building. The drift is premature-done across ten numbered clauses that a working solver does not exercise: pivot-count minimality, "must not create the output file ... and must not create the pivot log file when requested" on exception, "print the exact Python exception traceback to stderr", half-up rounding, positive-then-negative-then-zero term ordering. Blast radius is small (one package in /app), so not a 3.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes 120 sits at the top of the profile's ~30–120 minute band; agentTimeoutSec is 2500. Mandatory per-step stops are a noticeable fraction of a task this size, though not dominant. Scored consistently with B3=1.
evidence.C4: The instruction enumerates every artifact and the transformation between them: the exact CLI argument list and an example invocation, the algorithm by name ("two-phase simplex", "slack for <=, surplus plus artificial for >=, and artificial only for ="), the tableau column order, the pivot-log JSON Lines schema, the problem-report line-by-line format, and the degeneracy rule. Starter files are named and provided. No supplied input needs inspecting before the approach can be chosen.

rows.processRecommendation: library/methodologies/tdd.js composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js and library/processes/shared/completeness-gate.js (one gate per numbered clause, especially the exception-path and pivot-minimality requirements)
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent implements a correct two-phase simplex with Bland's or Dantzig's rule, verifies its own example invocation produces a sane optimal tableau, and declares done — silently failing §3's requirement that the logged pivot count be \"the smallest possible among all valid paths\" (the instruction warns fixed rules do not achieve it) and §10's requirement that no output, degeneracy, problem-report, basic-variable, or pivot-log file be created when an exception is raised, since a happy-path smoke run never exercises the error path or the --initial_pivots prefix.
rows.rationale: The decisive factor is B1: the instruction imposes a real internal artifact chain (construct Phase 1 tableau → apply the provided pivot prefix immediately → drop artificial columns at end of Phase 1 → Phase 2 → derive degeneracy and basic-variable reports from the final tableau), and getting that order wrong produces a plausible-looking but wrong tableau rather than a crash. B5 is unusually high for this corpus because the instruction states an explicit minimisation target (fewest pivot-log entries) with headroom that the agent can measure itself against. Cost is low: C4=0 because every artifact, schema, and the algorithm itself are enumerated up front, and C2 is only moderate at 120 expert-minutes. Drift risk is moderate rather than high — the schemas are exact and the diff is confined to one small package, but ten separate clauses (error-path file suppression, rounding, term ordering, pivot minimality) are each easy to leave unmet while a happy-path run looks green.

rows.name: coq-block-bound

evidence.B1: "You may add auxiliary definitions and lemmas anywhere in the file or in new `.v` files" — no step consumes a named earlier artifact. There is a natural reading order (inspect the declarations of `Triangle`, `path_valid`, `match_count`, `log2_nat`, then write the proof), and Coq requires lemmas be stated before use, but nothing downstream silently corrupts if the agent works in a different order; the compiler rejects order errors loudly.
evidence.B3: `expertMinutes: 960` (16 hours, 8x the corpus median of 120) and `agentTimeoutSec: 14400`, well above the 7200 anchor. The instruction itself states "You have 14400 seconds to complete this task." Far beyond one context window.
evidence.B5: The instruction names a self-runnable check: "The build command `coqc -Q . Top Main.v` (run from `/app/`) must exit with code 0." That is a locally reproducible pass/fail the agent can re-run, but it is binary — no numeric target, tolerance, or headroom to optimise toward. Partial progress (a chain of proved lemmas) is not scored by anything the instruction exposes.
evidence.B6: "You may add auxiliary definitions and lemmas anywhere in the file or in new `.v` files in `/app/`" permits splitting into lemma files, so decomposition is possible in principle, but the instruction enumerates exactly one deliverable — "Prove `target_theorem`" — and the lemma decomposition is itself the unknown part of the work, not a given fan-out of independently verifiable units.
evidence.B8: The instruction pre-emptively forbids the shortcuts an agent reaches for: "You must not modify the type signatures of ... or `target_theorem`" and "You must not introduce any new `Axiom`, `Parameter`, `Conjecture`, `Admitted`, or `admit.`" — enumerated prohibitions that name real premature-success paths. Latitude is wide ("anywhere in the file or in new `.v` files"), and over a 14400s budget the agent can accumulate a large body of auxiliary Coq that no longer serves the goal. Blast radius is bounded by the single build command and the small file surface, which keeps this off 3.
evidence.C2: `expertMinutes: 960` — over 8 hours, and a 14400s agent budget. Mandatory per-step stops are a rounding error against work of this size.
evidence.C4: The deliverable and its acceptance test are exact ("Prove `target_theorem` in `/app/Main.v`"; `coqc -Q . Top Main.v` exits 0), so the shape of the output is fully known, but the approach cannot be chosen until the supplied file named in the instruction is read — the statement of `target_theorem` and the definitions of `triangle_valid`, `path_valid`, `match_count` and `log2_nat` are not reproduced in the instruction. Tags `combinatorics`/`imo` imply the proof strategy is discovered rather than enumerated. Not 3: this is a stated deliverable, not a symptom requiring diagnosis.

rows.processRecommendation: custom — a proof-search convergence loop composing library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js (`coqc -Q . Top Main.v`), library/processes/shared/forbidden-markers-scanner.js (Axiom/Parameter/Conjecture/Admitted/admit.), library/processes/shared/prior-attempts-scanner.js (record refuted proof strategies across context windows), and library/processes/shared/n-strikes-escalation.js
rows.vanillaFailureMode: A vanilla session sinks most of its 14400s into one proof strategy for the combinatorial bound, runs out of context with a half-built lemma chain and no journal of which strategies were already refuted, then — to make something compile before stopping — closes the remaining holes with `admit.` or a fresh `Axiom`/`Parameter` and reports success; the instruction explicitly forbids exactly that, and nothing in a plain session forces a final `coqc -Q . Top Main.v` exit-0 run plus a forbidden-marker scan before the agent declares done.
rows.rationale: B3 is decisive: at 960 expert-minutes and a 14400s agent budget this task provably spans multiple context windows, and the single thing a vanilla session cannot carry across that boundary is the record of which proof strategies have already failed — which is precisely what an event-sourced journal and `genty resume` supply. C2 is 0 for the same reason, so the cost side is carried entirely by C4=2: the proof approach is genuinely undiscoverable until `/app/Main.v` is read, so any process encoded up front can govern the loop but not the mathematics. B1 is low because the instruction imposes no artifact chain — Coq's own compiler catches ordering mistakes — and B5 is only 1 because `coqc` exit-0 is binary with no measurable headroom, so a convergence loop has nowhere to converge except pass/fail. B8=2 rests on the instruction's own enumerated prohibitions against `admit.` and new `Axiom`s, which name the premature-success path directly and are cheaply enforceable as a scanner gate; the tight single-file surface and exact build command keep drift from being worse. Difficulty alone is not doing work in these scores — the horizon and the resumability it forces are.

rows.name: ctr-optimization

evidence.B1: The instruction imposes a hard, time-chained sequence: "Each config change to the ad campaign incurs a 15min dead period (in simulated hours) while the new params take effect", "the campaign must maintain at least 38 hours of airtime across the 48 hour campaign", and "No config change can be made during the evaluation period; any attempt will result in immediate failure." Parameter setting must also follow analysis of the impression stream, which "reflects all traffic the site receives, including both human and non-human" — the genuine-vs-bot classification is an intermediate artifact the parameter choice consumes. Acting out of order (tuning before deconfounding traffic, or changing config after hour 42) yields a plausible-but-failing result.
evidence.B3: "a simulated 48 hour period (each simulated hour lasts 360 seconds)" = 17,280 s of forced wall-clock, against "You have 18000 seconds to complete this task" and metadata agentTimeoutSec 18000 (far above the 7200 threshold), expertMinutes 288. The run is a multi-phase watch: explore traffic → infer genuine CTR → configure → let dead period settle → freeze before hour 42 → 6-hour evaluation window the agent must survive without touching anything.
evidence.B5: "the genuine user click-through rate (CTR) averages at least 2.2% during the evaluation window from hour 42 through hour 48" — an explicit numeric target the agent can measure itself against using the impression stream the API exposes, with an explicit explore/exploit loop (tags: "exploration-exploitation") and headroom to iterate on parameters during hours 0–42.
evidence.B6: "set the ad delivery parameters" (plural, enumerated in the OpenAPI spec at /openapi.json) plus a separable analysis sub-problem (fraud/bot filtering vs. parameter tuning). But there is a single campaign and a single shared simulation clock, and "Each config change ... incurs a 15min dead period" forces strict serialization — no real fan-out.
evidence.B8: The goal is stated as an outcome, not a deliverable, leaving wide latitude across a ~5-hour live simulation. Two named traps invite premature success: the stream is "the raw event log, which reflects all traffic ... including both human and non-human" (agent optimizes the inflated raw CTR and declares done), and the airtime/eval-window rules where "any attempt will result in immediate failure." Blast radius is unrecoverable in-run: simulated hours consumed by over-exploration or an extra dead period cannot be reclaimed.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes 288 (~4.8 h) and agentTimeoutSec 18000 place this in the 2–8 hour band: orchestration turns are material but do not dominate, and much of the wall-clock is spent waiting on the 360 s-per-simulated-hour clock, during which mandatory stops cost essentially nothing.
evidence.C4: The deliverable (a final campaign config) is named, but the approach cannot be chosen until supplied inputs named in the instruction are inspected: "The OpenAPI spec is served at the server's /openapi.json path" (which parameters even exist is unknown) and the impression stream, whose human/non-human separation method must be discovered from the data (tag: "fraud-detection"). The overall phase shape — probe, classify, tune, freeze — is knowable up front, so this is not a pure diagnosis task.

rows.processRecommendation: library/methodologies/state-machine-orchestration.js composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js and n-strikes-escalation.js — the deadline-phased explore/exploit/freeze structure is a good fit, but the airtime budget and the hard "no changes after hour 42" invariant would need a custom guard step.
rows.vanillaFailureMode: A vanilla session computes CTR straight off the raw event log — which the instruction warns includes non-human traffic — tunes parameters until that inflated number clears 2.2%, and stops; genuine CTR in hours 42–48 lands below target. The second concrete failure is clock drift: with no enforced step boundaries over ~4.8 hours of real time, the agent burns simulated hours on analysis, either dropping below the 38-hour airtime floor through repeated 15-minute dead periods or issuing one last "improvement" config change after hour 42, which the instruction says causes immediate failure.
rows.rationale: The decisive factor is the instruction's hard timing schedule: a 15-minute dead period per config change, a 38-of-48-hour airtime floor, and an evaluation window where "any attempt [to change config] will result in immediate failure" — a strict phase order whose violation is fatal and which a free-running agent can easily lose track of across 17,280 seconds of real wall-clock (B1=3, B3=3). The 2.2% genuine-CTR target gives a measurable objective with headroom and an explicit explore/exploit loop, so scored iteration has somewhere to go (B5=3), and drift risk is high because the instruction deliberately plants the raw-log confound that invites a premature, bot-inflated "done" (B8=3). Costs are modest: at ~288 expert-minutes the orchestration overhead is a small fraction of the work (C2=1), and the phase shape is knowable up front even though the specific parameters and bot-detection method require inspecting the OpenAPI spec and the event stream first (C4=2). Decomposability is the one weak benefit — the single campaign and serialized dead periods rule out fan-out (B6=1). Top benefit driver B1, top cost driver C4.

rows.name: cumulative-layout-shift

evidence.B1: The instruction states a single goal — "Eliminate cumulative layout shift from the website at /app/barber-shop-site/" — with no named intermediate artifact and no step that consumes an earlier step's output. There is a natural reading order (measure CLS, locate the shifting code, fix, re-measure) but deviating from it does not silently corrupt anything; the measurement is repeatable at any point.
evidence.B3: metadata.expertMinutes = 360 (6 hours, well above the corpus median of 120) and agentTimeoutSec = 10800, at/above the 7200 anchor for score 2. The site spans six route pages (app/page.tsx, about, services, gallery, book, socials) plus ~40 components and a separate backend container ('multi-container' tag).
evidence.B5: "All pages should measure zero CLS" is a stated numeric target on a continuous metric with headroom from a nonzero baseline, and the repo ships an agent-usable measurement path (barber-shop-site/.claude/skills/agent-browser/SKILL.md) so the agent can run measure-locate-fix-remeasure cycles per page rather than waiting on the hidden verifier.
evidence.B6: Six independent routes (app/page.tsx, app/about, app/services, app/gallery, app/book, app/socials), each measurable for CLS alone, plus separable shift sources (announcement-banner.tsx, promo-banner.tsx, gallery-grid.tsx, team-preview-loader.tsx, public/scripts/engage.js). Fan-out is real but partly coupled through the shared app/layout.tsx, globals.css and font loading, so not full independence.
evidence.B8: The instruction grants wide latitude — "You may change, replace, inline, or neutralize layout-shifting code, including third-party-style scripts" — while imposing preservation constraints that are easy to violate: "preserves the same visible elements, styling, and analytics side effects". The blast radius is the whole app (app/, components/, hooks/, globals.css, public/scripts/engage.js), and the cheapest route to zero CLS (deleting or fully disabling the banner/promo/analytics scripts) is exactly what the DOM-integrity and visual-comparison checks are there to catch.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes = 360 sits in the ~2–8 hour band; per-step orchestration stops are material but do not dominate six hours of profiling and editing across six pages.
evidence.C4: The instruction states a symptom/goal — "Eliminate cumulative layout shift" — rather than naming deliverables or transformations. No file, component, or fix is enumerated; the first real step is diagnosis: measuring per-page CLS and tracing each shift to its source (font swap, unsized media, late-injected banner, third-party engage.js). Any process fixed in advance would be guessing which sources exist and how many.

rows.processRecommendation: library/specializations/performance-optimization/ (task-level CLS/Core-Web-Vitals process) composed with library/processes/shared/playwright-visual-smoke.js and library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js; if no CLS-specific process exists, custom with an iterative-convergence loop keyed on per-page CLS plus a DOM/visual-parity gate on every iteration
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent fixes the homepage's obvious shifts, sees CLS reach zero on `/`, and stops without re-measuring /about, /services, /gallery, /book and /socials; or it neutralizes public/scripts/engage.js outright, which zeroes CLS but drops the analytics side effects and DOM nodes the instruction requires preserved.
rows.rationale: The decisive tension is a genuinely high-latitude, high-blast-radius fix (B8=3: the instruction permits neutralizing third-party scripts while demanding preserved visible elements, styling and analytics side effects) sitting on top of a goal-shaped instruction whose shape cannot be encoded until the site is profiled (C4=3). Enforcement would buy a per-page completeness gate and a preservation gate on every iteration — exactly the two ways a vanilla run fails here — but any process written before diagnosis would be guessing at the shift sources. B5=3 is well-evidenced: "All pages should measure zero CLS" is a measurable target with a baseline and an in-repo browser skill to measure against, so scored iterate-until-zero loops have somewhere to go. B3=2 from 360 expert-minutes and a 10800s agent timeout, with C2 correspondingly at 1. Benefit and cost land close together; the honest read is a hybrid — vanilla profiling to discover the shift inventory, then enforced fix-and-verify per page — rather than a clean route either way.

rows.name: data-anonymization

evidence.B1: 'References to the same underlying entity must produce the same token across all files, including across type-2 history rows, across transitively composing effective-dated subject merges, and across the transitive cross-tenant equivalences asserted in subject_links.csv.' The canonical entity-resolution map (transitive closure over merges + links) is an intermediate artifact that the per-row transform step consumes; emitting tokens before that closure exists yields a plausible-but-wrong result. Implied by artifact flow rather than enumerated as explicit phases, so not 3.
evidence.B3: metadata expertMinutes: 1440 (24 hours), far above the ~8-hour band; verifierTimeoutSec: 7200. The instruction also chains sub-deliverables (policy parsing, entity linkage, streaming transform, seed determinism, memory bound).
evidence.B5: '--max-memory 64MB' and 'peak memory must stay within --max-memory', plus 'Output must be deterministic for a given --seed, seeded transforms must change when the seed changes' — numeric/binary targets the agent can measure itself against and correct toward, but no optimisation headroom beyond clearing the ceiling.
evidence.B6: 'anonymizes the related CSV files in /app/input' with 'each policy column transformed per its policy' — per-column transforms are mildly separable, but the files are explicitly *related* (cross-file token consistency) and the deliverable is a single /app/anon.py, so there is little genuine fan-out.
evidence.B8: Output shape is pinned tightly ('preserve filenames, headers, column order, row order, and row counts') and there is one deliverable file, limiting blast radius; but several requirements fail invisibly — transitive merge/link closure, seed sensitivity, and the 64MB peak-memory ceiling — so the agent can ship output that looks correct and declare done.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes: 1440 — at ~24 hours of expert work, mandatory per-step stops are a rounding error against the work itself.
evidence.C4: The deliverable and exact CLI invocation are given ('python3 /app/anon.py /app/input --policy /app/policy.yaml --output /app/output --seed 42 --max-memory 64MB'), but the transform set cannot be chosen until /app/policy.yaml is read, and the linkage semantics not until /app/input and subject_links.csv are inspected — inputs named in the instruction that must be examined before the approach is fixed.

rows.processRecommendation: library/specializations/data-engineering-analytics/ composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js — gates: run twice with the same seed and diff, run with a changed seed and assert the diff is non-empty, assert header/column/row-order/row-count preservation, measure peak RSS against 64MB
rows.vanillaFailureMode: A vanilla agent hashes each policy column value in place per file, which satisfies 'same value -> same token' and produces output that survives eyeballing, but it never materialises the transitive closure over the effective-dated subject merges and subject_links.csv, so two rows naming one entity under different tenant keys get different tokens. The second likely silent failure is reading the frames into memory (pandas read_csv), blowing the 64MB peak-memory ceiling that the agent never actually measures before declaring success.
rows.rationale: The decisive factor is horizon: at 1440 expert-minutes this sits at the top of the corpus range, so orchestration overhead is negligible (C2=0) while resumability and enforced checkpoints have real value. Second is the implied artifact chain — the transitive entity-resolution map must exist before any token is emitted (B1=2) — combined with the fact that the requirements most likely to be silently skipped (cross-tenant transitivity, seed sensitivity, the 64MB bound) are each machine-checkable and would make sound step gates. Drift risk is moderate rather than high because the output contract is stated exactly and there is one deliverable file; decomposability is low because cross-file token consistency makes the CSVs one coupled unit. Cost is carried almost entirely by C4=2: the deliverable is pinned but the transform set is unknowable until policy.yaml and the inputs are read, so a short vanilla scouting read of those files should precede any encoded process.

rows.name: distributed-dedup

evidence.B1: The instruction names a chain of intermediate artifacts each consumed by the next: "find all pairs whose shingle-set Jaccard similarity meets the configured threshold, cluster them by connected components, and select one canonical representative per cluster", with shingling defined upstream ("Form the set of distinct contiguous shingleK-grams"). Producing representatives or clusters before the pair set is correct silently yields plausible-but-wrong output (e.g. clusterId not the true lowest docId of a transitively-connected component). Scored 2 rather than 3 because this is data-flow internal to one algorithm that any implementation naturally follows, not a workflow an agent is likely to invert.
evidence.B3: metadata expertMinutes: 600 (10 hours, well over the ~8h band and 5x the corpus median of 120) and agentTimeoutSec: 18000, far above the 7200 anchor. The instruction itself says "You have 18000 seconds to complete this task." Correctness implementation plus four separate resource-budget tunings is many phases over multiple context windows.
evidence.B5: Explicit numeric targets with headroom and an implied measure-and-improve loop: "wall-clock latency at most 1.5x the reference, peak executor memory at most 1.2x, join-operator output rows at most 1.2x, shuffle bytes read and written at most 1.2x". The harness ships PerformanceProfiler.scala, JoinSizeCapture.scala and SparkMetricsCollector.scala, so the agent can measure each of these itself and iterate (e.g. tune LSH band/row counts to cut candidate-pair volume) rather than guess.
evidence.B6: "Implement your solution by editing /app/submission/src/main/scala/tb/dedup/submission/SubmissionDedup.scala. Do not modify files outside that single source file" — one indivisible artifact. The internal stages (shingling, candidate generation, connected components, representative selection) are sequentially dependent and share one Spark plan, so they are not independently verifiable fan-out units.
evidence.B8: Output is exactly pinned ("columns docId (Long), clusterId (Long, the lowest docId in the cluster), and isRepresentative (Boolean)", "Exactly one output row per input doc") and the diff is one file, which bounds blast radius. But the instruction leaves the whole method open while imposing prohibitions that are easy to violate unnoticed — "Do not pull data to the driver, broadcast joins, use Cartesian products, or escape to the RDD API" (Spark's iterative connected-components idiom is normally RDD/GraphX, and checkpointing patterns tempt driver collection) — and correctness on a 10k corpus can pass while all four resource budgets are blown, inviting a premature "done".
evidence.C2: expertMinutes: 600 and agentTimeoutSec: 18000 put this far above the ~8-hour anchor; per-step mandatory stops are a rounding error against a ten-hour distributed-systems implementation with an iterative performance-tuning phase.
evidence.C4: The deliverable, trait signature, config defaults, tokenization rule ("text.toLowerCase.split(\"\\s+\")"), shingling edge cases ("If a doc has 0 < n < shingleK tokens..."), output schema and prohibited constructs are all enumerated up front — the shape is known. What is open is the method: the tags ("minhash", "lsh", "connected_components") name the standard approach for this domain, so only the algorithmic/tuning choices remain, and the reference implementation is hidden so the budget margins must be discovered empirically.

rows.processRecommendation: library/specializations/data-engineering-analytics/ composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js (correctness gate on the multiset-equality validator) and library/methodologies/iterative-convergence (separate scored loop per resource budget: latency 1.5x, memory 1.2x, join rows 1.2x, shuffle bytes 1.2x), plus a forbidden-markers-scanner pass for RDD API / broadcast / collect usage. Nearest single fit is custom.
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent gets a correct-but-naive implementation (full shingle inverted-index self-join over the 10k corpus) passing the exact-Jaccard multiset check, sees green, and declares done — never running the profiler to compare join-operator output rows and shuffle bytes against the 1.2x reference budget, so the submission fails on resources despite being correct. The parallel failure is the connected-components stage: an agent reaching for the familiar GraphX/RDD iterative idiom silently violates \"Do not ... escape to the RDD API\", which no correctness check surfaces.
rows.rationale: The decisive factor is horizon combined with a genuine convergence target: 600 expert-minutes and an 18000-second agent budget put this beyond any single sitting, and the four stated numeric budgets (1.5x latency, 1.2x memory, 1.2x join rows, 1.2x shuffle bytes) give a measure-and-improve loop somewhere to go rather than a binary pass. Cost is unusually low for this corpus — C2 is zero because ten hours of work dwarfs orchestration stops, and C4 is 1 because the instruction pins the trait, tokenization, edge cases, output schema and prohibited APIs, leaving only the standard minhash/LSH method choice open. B6 is low: one file, one sequentially-dependent Spark plan, no real fan-out. B8 is 2 rather than 3 — the exact output schema constrains the agent tightly, but correctness can pass while the resource budgets and the no-RDD prohibition are silently violated, which is exactly the premature-done failure named in the counterfactual. Scored per the profile with B2/B4/B7/C3/C5/C6 pinned and no verdict assigned.

rows.name: embedding-drift-monitor

evidence.B1: "compares incoming embedding windows against a reference baseline using KS, PSI, and MMD tests, then emits alerts through a debouncer" plus "Fix all the production modules ... not just the alert layer. The statistical and distance utilities have defects too." The alert layer consumes the output of the statistical/distance layer, so tuning the debouncer before the underlying statistics are correct produces a plausible-but-wrong calibration that must be redone; diagnose-then-fix-bottom-up is the ordering that matters.
evidence.B3: metadata expertMinutes: 300 (~5 hours) and agentTimeoutSec: 7200 — the profile's B3=2 band is "~2-8 hours, or an [agent] timeout_sec at/above 7200".
evidence.B5: "`/app/data/` has the reference embeddings and a handful of `.npy` files for different current-window scenarios" — the agent can self-run stable vs. drifted scenarios as a sanity check, but the instruction states no numeric threshold, tolerance, or target to converge toward.
evidence.B6: "Fix all the production modules under `/app/drift_monitor/`" spanning three named statistical tests (KS, PSI, MMD), the distance utilities, and the debouncer — several defect sites in distinct modules, each checkable on its own, though they share one package and one verifier.
evidence.B8: The instruction is symptom-level ("It's broken. Stable distributions trigger alerts they shouldn't, real drift goes undetected, and the alert state flickers") and explicitly anticipates a premature stop: "not just the alert layer. The statistical and distance utilities have defects too." No output schema or file list constrains the edit, so the agent can either stop at the first fixed symptom or rewrite the statistical modules wholesale.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes: 300 falls in the profile's ~2-8 hour band — orchestration turns are material but do not dominate five hours of debugging work.
evidence.C4: The instruction names symptoms rather than deliverables — "It's broken", "alert state flickers across windows in ways that don't track the underlying data" — and never says which module holds which defect or what the correct KS/PSI/MMD behaviour should be. The first real step is diagnosis across the whole package, so any pre-encoded phase list is a guess.

rows.processRecommendation: library/cradle/bugfix.js (diagnose-before-fix per module) composed with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js
rows.vanillaFailureMode: The agent fixes the most visible symptom — the debouncer's flickering alert state — tunes it until the stable `.npy` scenario stops firing, and declares the task done, leaving the KS/PSI/MMD implementations and the distance utilities with their original defects. The instruction's explicit warning ("not just the alert layer") is exactly the failure a single session drifts into, and the resulting monitor passes the agent's own spot-check while still missing real drift.
rows.rationale: The decisive tension is a genuine multi-layer debugging job (B3=2 at 300 expert-minutes and a 7200s timeout, B6=2 across statistics, distance, and alert modules) set against an instruction that gives only symptoms, which pins C4 at the top of the ladder. Enforcement has something real to enforce here — the bottom-up ordering (B1=2) and the named premature-stop failure the instruction itself warns against (B8=2) are exactly what mandatory stops and a completeness gate address. But the shape of the fix is not knowable until the package is read, so any process encoded up front is guesswork, and C4=3 dominates the cost side. B5 stays at 1: scenario files give a self-runnable sanity check but no stated numeric target, so there is no scored loop to converge along. Benefit_live ≈ 60.9 against Cost_live ≈ 70.5 puts this modestly negative; a hybrid — vanilla diagnosis to enumerate the defects, then enforced per-module fixing — is the honest reading.

rows.name: erp-procurement-planning

evidence.B1: "The final lineage must be either SO -> PO or SO -> MO -> (subassembly MO if needed) -> PO" plus origin rules: finished-goods POs carry the SO reference, component POs carry the MO reference, subassembly MOs carry the parent MO reference. Each document consumes an identifier produced by the previous one, so creating them out of order yields documents whose Source field cannot be filled correctly.
evidence.B3: metadata: expertMinutes 240 (4 hours), agentTimeoutSec 3600; the ladder puts ~2-8 hours at 2. The instruction also has distinct phases whose outputs feed each other: read /workspace/customer_order_requests.csv, gather Odoo notes/lead times/capacities, decide buy-vs-make, then create and confirm SOs, MOs and POs.
evidence.B5: "the portfolio-level new-spend margin stays at or above 28.1% at selling price, while staying within each customer's budget" combined with "minimizing any new procurement and manufacturing spend" — an explicit numeric threshold the agent can compute itself plus an optimisation objective with headroom, so measure-and-improve cycles over the buy/make mix have somewhere to go.
evidence.B6: Multiple customer orders and several document types ("sales orders, purchase orders, and/or manufacturing orders"), but the units are not independent: "Treat each workcenter's capacity as a hard horizon-wide limit shared across all products", "min/max quantities apply to the entire planning period", "one consolidated PO per supplier offer" and a portfolio-level margin couple the orders into one joint plan.
evidence.B8: "All notes, comments, and internal notes recorded on stock items, customers, vendors, and workcenters in Odoo are authoritative and must be respected" — constraints are scattered across records the agent must go find, and it writes and confirms many ERP documents (SOs, MOs, work orders, POs with dates). Confirmed documents across a live ERP are a wide surface and hard to review, though the required fields and lineage are exactly specified, which caps latitude.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes 240 places this in the ~2-8 hour band: orchestration stops are material but do not dominate several hours of data gathering, planning and document creation.
evidence.C4: Deliverables and fields are enumerated (which documents, which dates, which Source values), but the actual plan cannot be chosen until supplied inputs are inspected: /workspace/customer_order_requests.csv, per-workcenter Internal Notes for "the exact minute limit", vendor min/max and maximum order quantities, lead times. Whether to buy, manufacture, or mix is discovered from that data, not stated.

rows.processRecommendation: custom (plan-then-commit process wrapping library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js for the margin/budget/capacity checks, with library/methodologies/plan-and-execute.js as the skeleton)
rows.vanillaFailureMode: A vanilla agent fulfils every order and confirms the documents, then declares success without re-verifying the portfolio-level 28.1% new-spend margin against its final buy-vs-make mix, or without checking a workcenter's Internal-Notes minute limit against the total scheduled work orders. The artifacts look complete — every order has an SO, dates are set — but the plan silently violates the margin floor or over-books a workcenter, and component POs carry SO references in Source instead of the parent MO references because the POs were created before the MOs existed.
rows.rationale: The decisive live factor is B1: the instruction spells out a chained document lineage (SO -> MO -> subassembly MO -> PO) where each artifact's origin field references one produced earlier, so ordering violations silently yield a plausible-but-wrong document graph. B5 is also high — 28.1% margin, per-customer budgets and a "minimize new spend" objective are all self-measurable with headroom, so scored iteration has somewhere to go. Against that, C4=2 dominates the cost side: the deliverables are named precisely but the plan itself only emerges after reading the CSV, vendor min/max limits and workcenter Internal Notes, so a process encoded up front can fix the shape of the document flow but not the decisions. B6 is low because the shared capacity limit and portfolio-level margin couple all orders into one joint optimisation rather than independent units, and B8 is moderate — wide ERP write surface and scattered authoritative constraints, but exactly specified output fields.

rows.name: exam-pdf-eval

evidence.B1: Chained artifact flow stated explicitly: 'discovers every ... pair', then 'extracts each problem and its gold answer, formats each problem to the protocol, evaluates both models, parses the predicted letter, and writes extracted.jsonl, results.json, and raw_outputs.jsonl'. extracted.jsonl feeds the prompt formatting, which feeds raw_outputs.jsonl, which feeds results.json; and results_rerun.json is 'a second full run' that only means anything after the first run exists ('The two runs must produce identical predictions'). Formatting must also follow /paper/eval_protocol.md's 'unicode-substitution table, in-context exemplars, and decoding/parsing parameters' — doing inference before reading it silently yields plausible-but-wrong predictions that still validate against the schema.
evidence.B3: metadata expertMinutes = 840 (14 hours, over the profile's ~8-hour bar) and agentTimeoutSec = 14400 (well above 7200). The instruction itself states 'You have 14400 seconds to complete this task.' Distinct phases each producing a consumed artifact (extraction -> protocol formatting -> two-model inference -> results, then a full rerun).
evidence.B5: The instruction supplies a self-measurable target with headroom: '/paper/dev_predictions.json is a small dev set for the Qwen model' — the agent can score its own pipeline against it and iterate on the unicode table, exemplars and parsing until agreement rises. A second numeric constraint is stated and self-checkable: 'The harness must record its own end-to-end wall-clock runtime ... and that runtime must not exceed fifteen minutes per run', plus 'predictions must substantially agree with the reference'.
evidence.B6: The deliverable is one indivisible artifact: 'a self-contained evaluation harness as a single file at /app/harness.py'. There is mild internal fan-out (two models, two exams, four output files), but no set of independently verifiable units that could be worked in parallel.
evidence.B8: Output schemas are pinned line-by-line (exact JSON keys for extracted.jsonl, results.json, raw_outputs.jsonl), which constrains the agent tightly. Drift latitude comes from the generalization requirement the agent cannot check locally: verification 're-invokes /app/harness.py on one additional exam whose layout differs from the two you can see — booklets in the wild range from clean vector PDFs to image-only scans', and 'The grader's Python environment is exactly this container's pre-installed package set; packages you install yourself are not present there.' An agent can hardcode the two visible label/choice styles, pip-install an OCR dependency, produce four schema-valid files and declare success.
evidence.C2: expertMinutes = 840 (~14 hours) with agentTimeoutSec = 14400; mandatory per-step stops are a rounding error against work of this size.
evidence.C4: The instruction enumerates every output artifact and the transformation between them, and '/paper/eval_protocol.md documents the reference pipeline's unicode-substitution table, in-context exemplars, and decoding/parsing parameters', so the pipeline shape is given. Only the tooling is open — which PDF text-extraction/OCR route survives 'clean vector PDFs to image-only scans' is decided after inspecting the booklets, but that is a method choice inside a known shape.

rows.processRecommendation: custom — compose library/methodologies/spec-driven-development.js (spec from /paper/eval_protocol.md) with library/processes/shared/deterministic-quality-gate.js gating on dev-set agreement, the 15-minute wall-clock budget, and a run-vs-rerun prediction-identity check
rows.vanillaFailureMode: A vanilla session tunes the extractor to the two booklets it can see — hardcoding the `7.`/`Q-7` and `(A)`/`A)` variants it happens to observe — never builds the image-only/OCR fallback the instruction warns about, writes four schema-valid files, and declares done; the verifier's re-invocation on the held-out differently-laid-out exam then extracts zero or garbled problems. The second likely silent failure: decoding parameters are left non-greedy or unseeded, so `results_rerun.json` disagrees with `results.json` on a handful of problems, and the agent never runs the determinism comparison it was told to satisfy because the first run's numbers looked reasonable.
rows.rationale: Decisive factor is the chained artifact flow (B1=3) sitting on top of a 14-hour expert horizon (B3=3, agentTimeoutSec 14400): extraction feeds protocol-formatted prompts, which feed raw generations, which feed results, which must then be reproduced identically in a second run — each link can be silently wrong while every downstream file still validates against the stated schema. B5=3 is unusual for this corpus and real: dev_predictions.json and the fifteen-minute budget give the agent two things it can measure itself against and iterate on before the hidden verifier ever runs. Cost is near-floor — C2=0 because orchestration overhead is noise against 840 expert-minutes, and C4=1 because the instruction enumerates all four artifacts and /paper/eval_protocol.md documents the pipeline, leaving only the extraction/OCR tooling open. B8 is held at 2 rather than 3: the output schemas are pinned exactly, so the drift risk is not sprawl but the specific, locally-uncheckable generalization to the held-out layout plus the "packages you install yourself are not present" trap. B6=1 because the deliverable is explicitly a single file with no parallel fan-out.

rows.name: fin-saccr-rwa

evidence.B1: SA-CCR is an explicitly chained pipeline and the instruction names each link: trade-level "d_adj, delta, MF, and effective notional, then the hedging-set roll-up below the trades" feed the aggregate add-on; the add-on plus "replacement_cost_usd" feed "pfe_multiplier" and "pfe_usd"; those feed "ead_usd"; then "map the RWA with CRR3 SA-CR, and take the capital requirement as the usual 8% of RWA". Upstream inputs gate downstream terms: the "three collateral disputes ... that ran past the standard MPOR" must be resolved before the margined MF, and the amended "csa_terms.csv ... IA custody and segregation terms ... bear on the collateral treatment" before RC. Violating the order yields a plausible-but-wrong number, not a visible error.
evidence.B3: metadata expertMinutes: 480 (8 expert-hours, 4x the corpus median of 120) and agentTimeoutSec: 9000, above the 7200 anchor. The instruction also has distinct artifact-producing phases whose outputs the next consumes: per-trade workings -> hedging-set roll-up -> /app/output/sa_ccr_results.csv, plus a second deliverable /app/output/sa_ccr_workings.xlsx with "formulas intact".
evidence.B5: No numeric target, tolerance, or self-runnable check is stated. "Report every USD amount to exactly two decimals" is a formatting spec, not a target with headroom; correctness is binary against the hidden golden sa_ccr_results.csv, so a measure-and-improve loop has nowhere to climb.
